newsitem.title: USA: Celtrix finishes Phase I test of SomatoKine.
newsitem.headline: Celtrix finishes Phase I test of SomatoKine.

text.p: Celtrix Pharmaceuticals Inc on Monday said it has finished Phase I human clinical studies of SomatoKine showing positive results that have led it to begin feasibility studies for Phase II.

Data from the Phase I trial showed that repeated or continuous administration of SomatoKine safely delivers IGF-I at substantially higher dosage levels than have ever been feasible before, Celtrix said in a statement.
Also, SomatoKine increases peak blood concentration of IGF-I up to 35-times normal, and elevated levels of SomatoKine stimulate markers of bone and connective tissue metabolism.
"Based on these findings, we have initiated Phase II feasibility studies for our first treatment target, recovery from hip fracture," said Andreas Sommer, chief executive.
SomatoKine is the recombinant equivalent of the natural complex formed by insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I) and its major binding protein (BP3).
IGF-I is an anabolic hormone that plays a major role in diverse biological processes including muscle and bone formation and tissue repair.
Celtrix shares were up 5/16 at 2-9/16 by mid-afternoon.
